title: get_hist16's tail loop uses a raw high-bit-depth sample as a histogram index, so the bump lands outside the 256-entry sub-slice carved for that plane
object: one av_calloc holding nb_threads slices of 3*256 ints, carved twice by pointer arithmetic: hist = thread_histogram + HIST_SIZE * jobnr (:206), then hhist = hist + 256 * plane (:259)
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. Spatial, as every row of this corpus.
shape: the vectorised loop above shifts and masks the sample; the tail loop -- reached only when the width is not a multiple of 4, the 'odd sized HBD input' of the subject line -- does not, so a 10-bit sample up to 1023 indexes a 256-entry sub-slice
allocator_layer: FFmpeg's own carve, one level down from the allocation: av_calloc hands out ONE block (vf_thumbnail.c:337) and the filter carves it into per-thread slices and per-plane sub-slices by pointer arithmetic (:206, :259). The crossing leaves a sub-slice and stays in the block.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. HIST_SIZE (3*256) and the 256-entry per-plane stride are unreduced, as is the carve arithmetic. The sample is 10-bit, deliberately: a 16-bit sample would leave the allocation and the row would then be measuring a different boundary than the corpus's. get_hist16's vectorised body is left out because it is not the path that crosses -- the tail is, which is why the defect needs an odd width.
nested_why: the crossed region was made by FFmpeg's carving code, not by the allocator that handed out the block: under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- the object is the carved sub-slice, so the row is NESTED, as every carve in this corpus is. Until 2026-10-10 it was subobject-repros case 09 and marked NOT NESTED there, against the rule this corpus and tools/catch-tables.py state for carves.
note: Moved from capstone/bug-corpora/ffmpeg/subobject-repros/09_ac59fc542f_thumbnail_carved_histogram_slice (2026-10-10). Its readings there -- every arm of that corpus, on that harness -- stay in subobject-repros/results/; this case is re-measured in this corpus's harness, where the block is the platform's calloc and the carve is ffc_carve().
